banditlab

banditlab is an R framework for multi-armed bandit experimentation: simulating, comparing and extending sequential decision algorithms.

It provides:

  • Environments: Bernoulli, Gaussian, and arbitrary user-defined reward processes.
  • Policies: random, greedy (with optimistic initial values), epsilon-greedy (fixed and scheduled), explore-then-commit, UCB1 and Beta-Bernoulli Thompson sampling.
  • One experiment engine: replicated runs, one independent random number stream per replicate (results do not depend on how many replicates you run), and seed-paired policy comparisons by construction.
  • Explicit metrics: pseudo-regret with exact documented definitions (?regret_definitions), never computed when the environment cannot support them.
  • Tidy results: summaries, checkpoints and full trajectories as tibbles, sized deliberately (trajectories are opt-in).
  • Propensity-complete logs: every built-in stochastic policy logs the marginal probability of each selected action, the prerequisite for importance-weighted offline evaluation.
  • A small extension API: implement three S3 methods and your policy runs in the same engine as the built-ins (vignette("custom-policies")).

Why it exists

The only general bandit framework R has had, contextual, was archived from CRAN in 2021. What remains covers Bayesian A/B analysis and clinical trial designs, not general bandit experimentation. banditlab fills that gap with a deliberately small, tested, dependency-light core (tibble and ggplot2 are the only non-base imports).

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RProDigest/banditlab")

Once released on CRAN:

install.packages("banditlab")

In 60 seconds 

library(banditlab)

env <- bandit_bernoulli(c(low = 0.15, mid = 0.25, high = 0.40))

result <- run_experiment(
  env,
  policies = list(
    epsilon  = policy_epsilon_greedy(0.1),
    ucb      = policy_ucb1(),
    thompson = policy_thompson()
  ),
  horizon = 1000,
  replications = 50,
  seed = 42,
  checkpoints = seq(50, 1000, by = 50)
)

summary(result)
#> one row per policy: mean and quantiles of final cumulative regret,
#> mean reward, mean optimal-action share

autoplot(result, metric = "cumulative_regret")

Seed-paired comparison against a baseline:

cmp <- compare_policies(result, baseline = "epsilon")
aggregate(difference ~ policy, data = cmp, FUN = mean)

Telecoms case study

The article Bandits for RAN optimisation: 5G NR link adaptation uses banditlab to compare bandit policies with a static CQI rule and outer-loop link adaptation (OLLA) in simulated stationary and drifting radio conditions. It builds both industry baselines with the extension API, without modifying the package.

Extending

A custom policy is a constructor plus three S3 methods (policy_state(), select_arm(), update_state()). The vignette vignette("custom-policies") implements softmax exploration from scratch and runs it against the built-in policies; the package’s own test suite runs a policy implemented this way to guarantee the extension interface keeps working.

Relationship to the book

banditlab is the computational companion of the book in progress Adaptive Bandit Methods with R, which teaches the algorithms by building transparent implementations before introducing the package. The package is designed to stand alone: nothing in its documentation requires the book.

Development status

Version 0.1.0. The public API described in the reference and vignettes is intended to be stable; the extension generics (policy_state(), select_arm(), update_state()) are the package’s compatibility contract. Planned directions (non-stationary environments, contextual policies, offline evaluation) are listed in the repository’s roadmap.
